         1                 P R O C E E D I N G S

         2                  THE PRESIDENT:    The Senate will

         3       please come to order.

         4                  I ask everyone present to stand and

         5       recite with me the Pledge of Allegiance to our

         6       Flag.

         7                  (Whereupon, the assemblage recited

         8       the Pledge of Allegiance to the Flag.)

         9                  THE PRESIDENT:    Today's

        10       invocation will be provided by the Reverend

        11       Peter G. Young, from the Mother Teresa

        12       Community here in Albany.

        13                  REVEREND YOUNG:    Thank you,

        14       Governor.

        15                  Let us pray.

        16                  Almighty and Eternal God, You have

        17       revealed Your glory to all nations.  God of

        18       power and might, wisdom and justice comes to

        19       our Senators through Your authority and the

        20       prayer that Your laws are enacted and

        21       judgements are decreed, with our citizens

        22       benefiting from the dedication of our session

        23       today.

        24                  May we pray and thank God for those

        25       that have served in this Senate.  And may we



                      Candyco Transcription Service, Inc.
                                                         8423



         1       again thank them for their service, for their

         2       new careers.  And we again want to again

         3       welcome the new members.

         4                  And we would take a moment to

         5       remember, as a group, our Senator Morahan, who

         6       has passed since the last time that we've met,

         7       without an opportunity to thank God for this

         8       man.  May we pray for him now in a moment of

         9       silence.

        10                  Amen.

        11                  (Whereupon, the assemblage

        12       respected a moment of silence.)

        13                  THE PRESIDENT:    The Senate

        14       remains in extraordinary session.

        15                  The reading of the Journal.

        16                  The Secretary will read.

        17                  THE SECRETARY:    In Extraordinary

        18       Session Number II, the Senate met pursuant to

        19       adjournment.  The Journal of Saturday,

        20       November 27, was read and approved.  On

        21       motion, Senate adjourned.

        22                  THE PRESIDENT:    Without

        23       objection, the Journal stands approved as

        24       read.

        25                  Senator Klein.

         1                  SENATOR KLEIN:    Mr. President, I

         2       believe there's a concurrent resolution at the

         3       desk by Senator Sampson.  I ask that the title

         4       of the resolution be read and move for its

         5       immediate adoption.

         6                  THE PRESIDENT:    Senator Klein,

         7       has this resolution been deemed privileged and

         8       submitted by the office of the Temporary

         9       President?

        10                  SENATOR KLEIN:    Yes, it has,

        11       Mr. President.

        12                  THE PRESIDENT:    The Secretary

        13       will read.

        14                  THE SECRETARY:    By Senator

        15       Sampson, Concurrent Resolution Number 2,

        16       relative to the adjournment of the

        17       Extraordinary Session of the Legislature

        18       sine die.

        19                  THE PRESIDENT:    The question is

        20       on the concurrent resolution.  All those in

        21       favor please signify by saying aye.

        22                  (Response of "Aye.")

        23                  THE PRESIDENT:    Opposed?

        24                  (No response.)

        25                  THE PRESIDENT:    The concurrent



                      Candyco Transcription Service, Inc.
                                                         8425



         1       resolution is adopted.

         2                  Before this extraordinary session

         3       is adjourned, I would like to take the liberty

         4       of just saying a couple of personal words.

         5                  This has been an extraordinary

         6       experience for me in the last 15 months.  I

         7       deeply appreciate the courtesies that have

         8       been extended to me by I think almost each and

         9       every one of you.

        10                  I've enjoyed the opportunity to

        11       have had an impact on the gargantuan problems

        12       that this state faces.  I regret that I was

        13       not able to be more helpful in producing

        14       solutions.

        15                  I am constantly subjected to

        16       comments about how could I possibly have

        17       anything to do with such a dreadful body as

        18       the New York State Legislature.  And I want to

        19       tell you -- and I read that every day,

        20       practically, in the newspapers.  And I want to

        21       tell you that I appreciate the extraordinary

        22       difficulty, particularly of dealing with a

        23       body that's equally divided.

        24                  But I have to tell you I continue

        25       to believe that politics is not a dirty word,



                      Candyco Transcription Service, Inc.
                                                         8426



         1       it's the way that democracy makes decisions.

         2       And I think that each and every one of you in

         3       your own way care much more than you're given

         4       credit for for the well-being of the people of

         5       this state.

         6                  I know, because it's been a matter

         7       of great intellectual interest to me for

         8       thirty years, how serious the fiscal problems

         9       are and how difficult it is to make the

        10       changes that have to be made in the way

        11       benefits and burdens are allocated,

        12       particularly for people who have to run for

        13       election.

        14                  But I have a great underlying faith

        15       in the DNA of this country and of this state.

        16       I've lived here 77 years; I hope to be around

        17       a long time.  Between me, my children, and my

        18       grandchildren, we own nine homes in the State

        19       of New York, so I have a stake not just as a

        20       matter of passion and commitment, but also

        21       with that investment of most of our family's

        22       resources.

        23                  And I want to tell you something

        24       that I have found.  Despite the enormous

        25       frustrations, I have found this experience to



                      Candyco Transcription Service, Inc.
                                                         8427



         1       be fascinating, challenging.  I've made

         2       friends that I hope that I'm able to keep.

         3                  And as you all look to the future,

         4       I can only say I wish you the best of luck,

         5       and Godspeed, and thank you again for your

         6       courtesies.

         7                  Thank you.

         8                  (Standing ovation.)

         9                  THE PRESIDENT:    This

        10       extraordinary session is adjourned sine die.

        11                  (Whereupon, at 4:07 p.m., the

        12       Senate adjourned.)
